title: JUMP 'N BUMP
subtitle: Brainchild Design, 1998 · the original DOS/DJGPP source — unchained planar VGA at 400x256

needsData.hint: jumpbump.dat from the 1998 DOS release — NOT one repacked from the source tree's data/. The tree ships its packer (modify/pack.c) and it works, but the 2002 source release carries a different levelmap.txt from the game that shipped, so a rebuilt archive makes the rabbit swim on a solid platform. See _data.

_why: The first program on the shelf whose screen is NOT a buffer. Every other DOS game here draws into a linear framebuffer at 0xA0000 and the page reads it where it lies; this one runs unchained VGA -- mode X -- where four consecutive pixels live in four different planes and an address no longer denotes one place. That costs a paged image, a page map, a planar device, and a frame that is de-interleaved rather than published. Its frame boundary is a register write (the CRTC start address) rather than a function call, and it is also the first target whose assembly cannot be sidestepped: get_block and put_block are defined nowhere but dos/gfx.S, with no C twin anywhere in the tree.
_keys: Player one's keys are the ARROWS, and they are the reason the web keyboard learned about 0xE0. Set 1's software convention gives ArrowUp and Numpad8 the same code, 72, and every other program here is happy with that -- but this game's own vector-9 handler files an extended key at (code + 0x80), so its KEY_PL1_JUMP is 0xc8 and a bare 72 lands in a byte it never reads. The queue now carries the prefix flag beside the code, and this host sends the pair the hardware would.
_data: jumpbump.dat is the game's data, not PRISM's: it is named here and read from a directory the player points at, and it never enters the repository. Brainchild's own tarball is not recoverable -- the site serves an empty page and the Wayback Machine has jnb-src.zip only as a 404 -- so the source comes from the CVS import at the LibreGames repository's root commit, which is DOS with no platform guard to choose.
_the_source_release_is_not_the_shipped_g: AND THAT IS A TRAP THAT LOOKS LIKE AN EMULATION BUG. Repacking data/ from the 2002 source tree gives an archive whose 18 members are 15 identical to the 1998 release -- level.pcx among them -- and three not: levelmap.txt (382 bytes shipped, 367 in the tree), mask.pcx (5538 vs 5530) and calib.dat. levelmap.txt is the COLLISION map, loaded over the static table in main.c, and main.c reads value 2 as water (`ban_map[..] == 2` -> `in_water = 1`). Rows 9-11 at centre-right are 3 and 1 in the shipped map and 2 in the tree's, so with a rebuilt archive a rabbit swims in mid-air on a solid platform -- and every symptom points at the renderer, the planar device or the page map, none of which is wrong. Measured by extracting both archives and diffing them member by member; PRISM loaded each one's 352 cells unshifted in both cases.
_measured: 900 frames of the menu in 0.5 s, 1,894 rendered frames/s on the deterministic clock; 400x256, 100 bytes a row per plane, 55,481 non-zero pixels of 102,400 in 101 colours. Keyboard measured against the game's own keyb[] and against the first frame at which the picture diverges: 61, one frame after the tap.
